developer_request: Prepare an independently installable artifact that honestly supports every capability advertised by its install profile, including any optional validation/developer bundle. Do not infer artifact completeness from the source checkout working.
known_facts: The parent-reply install profile advertises an optional devtest bundle as 63 regression cases plus 54 safety-gate cases for secondary development or acceptance.
That devtest bundle includes only the parent-reply/_test directory.
The bundled _test/run_regression.py requires a sibling g2_regression_cases.json at runtime.
The actual _test directory does not contain g2_regression_cases.json, so the advertised installed regression runner is not dependency-closed even before model/API availability is considered.

Current canonical verification has also moved to top-level tests/parent-reply plus tests/framework, so a source-tree green result would not by itself prove the independently installed devtest artifact is current or executable.
expected_first_moves: identify the capabilities the final install/package/container/zip claims to provide, including optional profiles rather than only the default path
inspect the final artifact/install plan for all files, runtime dependencies, entrypoints, configuration, and externally declared prerequisites required by each claimed capability
exercise representative capability paths from the built/installed artifact in a clean target rather than from the source checkout when the artifact boundary is material
if an optional capability is not closed, either make that artifact slice self-contained/dependency-declared or stop advertising/installing the capability until it is valid
keep source-tree verification and artifact verification as distinct evidence claims
must_preserve: valid source-tree development tests as source-tree evidence
honest optional artifact profiles that may intentionally omit capabilities
declared external dependencies when they are explicit and verifiably resolvable
the ability to ship a smaller core artifact when optional developer/test tooling is not part of that artifact's contract
must_not: treat source checkout success as proof that a built or installed artifact is dependency-closed
claim an optional validation/developer capability when required files or entrypoints are absent from the installed artifact
hide missing artifact dependencies behind the developer machine's source tree, global environment, or leftover files
force every project to bundle tests or development tooling when those capabilities are not part of the accepted artifact contract
copy this consumer's Python paths, Skill names, or test counts into AAOP Core
lessons: Source-tree success, build success, artifact success, installation success, runtime success, and accepted target outcome are separate evidence layers.

A release/install artifact must be closed for the capabilities it actually claims: required files, runtime dependencies, entrypoints, configuration, and declared external prerequisites must survive the artifact boundary.
Optional artifact profiles need their own closure evidence; a broken optional developer/test bundle must not inherit the source repository's green status.
Representative validation should execute from the final built/installed artifact in a clean target when artifact boundaries are material.
